{{short description|Collinearity of the midpoints of parallel chords in a conic}}
In [[geometry]], the '''midpoint theorem''' describes a property of parallel [[Chord (geometry)|chord]]s in a [[Conic section|conic]]. It states that the midpoints of parallel chords in a conic are located on a common line.

The common line or line segment for the midpoints is called the [[diameter]]. For a [[circle]], [[ellipse]] or [[hyperbola]] the diameter goes through its [[centre (geometry)#Projective conics|center]]. For a [[parabola]] the diameter is always perpendicular to its [[Conic section#Eccentricity, focus and directrix|directrix]] and for a pair of intersecting lines (from a [[degenerate conic]]) the diameter goes through the point of intersection.
